results.content: # Strategic insights for entrepreneurship and business growth in the export sector. + Published by Springer Nature in International Entrepreneurship and Management Journal. Santander – Colombia in one of the most important department of the country due to the latest measurement in competitiveness index, this study offers a comprehensive analysis of Santander, Colombia’s export sector from 2010 to 2020, utilizing regional opportunity map data to identify trends and growth patterns. Examining 128 exporting firms in 2020 through a financial analysis and multiple linear regression, the research establishes key variables influencing business growth. The model showed statistical significance, indicating the impact of explanatory variables on firm growth. Notably, company size directly affects growth, while higher current ratios and levels of indebtedness inversely correlate with sales revenue. Providing insights into Santander’s export dynamics, the study informs strategies for future development, considering post-pandemic impacts and opportunities from ongoing Free Trade Agreement negotiations. Its contribution lies in its decade-long examination of the export sector, using financial and regression approaches to elucidate the relationship between company size, economic activity, financial indicators, and business growth, while also anticipating the implications of future trade agreements for the region. results.title: Strategic insights for entrepreneurship and business growth in the export sector | International Entrepreneurship and Management Journal | Springer Nature Link
results.content: Santander – Colombia in one of the most important department of the country due to the latest measurement in competitiveness index, this study offers a comprehensive analysis of Santander, Colombia’s export sector from 2010 to 2020, utilizing regional opportunity map data to identify trends and growth patterns. Its contribution lies in its decade-long examination of the export sector, using financial and regression approaches to elucidate the relationship between company size, economic activity, financial indicators, and business growth, while also anticipating the implications of future trade agreements for the region. In the study of exporting companies in Santander (Colombia), authors propose internationalisation strategies related to: the development of products or services of international stature, investment and negotiation processes with destination countries, and also the manager’s attitude towards managing uncertainty when promoting internationalisation as a valid business strategy (Mujica & Velasco, 2016. The significant variables that explain the business growth of exporting firms in Santander are size, current ratio, debt level, whether the firm is a limited joint-stock, and whether the firm belongs to the Wholesale and retail trade, repair of motor vehicles and motorbikes sector.
